macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: US stocks finish mixed as bonds and rate expectations weigh
items.summary: The Dow fell 443.87 points, or 0.86%, while the S&P 500 also declined; the Nasdaq gained as technology shares rallied. Cooler-than-expected inflation data reduced expectations for another near-term Federal Reserve rate hike, but elevated Treasury yields pressured broader equities.

items.title: Asian markets mixed after Wall Street selloff
items.summary: Asian stocks traded unevenly as positive US economic data supported sentiment, while elevated government-bond yields and oil prices remained headwinds. Investors were also weighing cooler US inflation against stronger economic-growth data.

items.title: Micron reports strong earnings and outlook
items.summary: Micron exceeded fourth-quarter revenue and profit expectations and issued a strong first-quarter outlook, boosting technology shares. The company also warned that narrower margins could temper the benefit of strong demand.

items.title: Cooler inflation reduces pressure for near-term Fed tightening
items.summary: The latest reading of the Federal Reserve’s preferred personal-consumption-expenditures inflation gauge came in below forecasts at 3.4%, helping traders reduce bets on another immediate rate hike. Revised second-quarter growth was stronger, supported by investment related to artificial intelligence.

items.title: Japan data points to continued BOJ tightening debate
items.summary: Japan’s manufacturing PMI reached 54.1 in September, while Tankan manufacturing sentiment improved but slightly missed expectations. Recent Bank of Japan commentary and opinion summaries increased speculation about additional rate hikes.

items.title: US market session awaits jobs and manufacturing data
items.summary: US investors are scheduled to receive weekly initial jobless claims, September ISM manufacturing data, and August construction-spending figures. Accenture, Nike, and McCormick are among the major companies reporting earnings.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin enters October near $83,500 as ETF flows turn negative
items.summary: Bitcoin traded near $83,500 after briefly rising above $85,000, while U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $148.69 million in outflows on September 30 after $2.65 billion of net inflows during September. Rising Treasury yields continued to weigh on risk assets.

items.title: Crypto hacks reportedly reach $768 million in September
items.summary: September was described as the worst month for cryptocurrency exploits in 2026, with reported losses exceeding $768 million. The figure highlights continued security risks across crypto protocols and applications.

items.title: U.K. FCA opens applications for full crypto authorization
items.summary: The Financial Conduct Authority opened a window for crypto firms to apply for authorization under the U.K.’s forthcoming regulatory regime. Applications are due by February 28, 2027, while the new regime is scheduled to begin on October 25, 2027.

items.title: Moca Chain mainnet launches with verifiable credentials
items.summary: Animoca Brands’ Moca Foundation and Moca Network launched the Moca Chain mainnet, designed to let users and AI agents share verifiable credentials across applications. The network also introduced AIR as an entry point for businesses to access users and agents.

items.title: XRP Ledger passes 10 million x402 payments
items.summary: The XRP Ledger surpassed 10 million payments through the x402 protocol, less than three months after reaching 1 million. AI agents paying for computing and data reportedly account for most of the activity.

items.title: MEXC doubles Guardian Fund Bitcoin holdings to 2,000 BTC
items.summary: MEXC added 1,000 Bitcoin to its Guardian Fund, bringing the fund’s holdings to 2,000 BTC. The fund also reportedly holds 100 million USDT, with its wallet address available for on-chain verification.

items.title: Bloomberg launches institutional stablecoin data dashboard
items.summary: Bloomberg launched a Terminal dashboard providing data on stablecoin supply, issuance and transaction activity. The dashboard was developed with Allium to give financial professionals direct access to on-chain stablecoin metrics.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Google unveils Gemini 4 Argon frontier model
items.summary: Google introduced Gemini 4 Argon, a new frontier model focused on complex workflows, coding, and cybersecurity. Initial access is limited to selected cybersecurity partners and trusted testers through the Fairwind program, with broader availability not yet scheduled.

items.title: Anthropic reportedly launches Opus 5.5
items.summary: Anthropic launched Opus 5.5, described as its first major model release since CEO Dario Amodei called for a slowdown in AI development. The release adds to intensifying competition among leading frontier-model providers.

items.title: ElevenLabs valuation more than doubles to $22 billion
items.summary: AI voice startup ElevenLabs reportedly more than doubled its valuation to $22 billion through a share sale, placing it among the most highly valued AI companies and highlighting continued investor demand for generative-audio businesses.

items.title: Bank of England governor warns about autonomous AI risks
items.summary: The Bank of England governor warned that increasingly autonomous and potentially self-improving AI systems pose significant risks and urged stronger efforts to bring them under control.

items.title: Micron raises outlook amid AI memory demand
items.summary: Micron forecast quarterly revenue of approximately $61.5 billion, above the analyst consensus cited in coverage, reflecting continued strong demand for memory technology used by AI-chip and data-center operators.
